title: Fibrant simplicial groupoids model all spaces
statement: Use the infinity-category and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Use coherent nerves, locally Kan simplicial categories, and Dwyer–Kan equivalences as in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. A simplicial groupoid is a simplicial object in ordinary groupoids with constant set of objects; its arrows have strict degreewise inverses compatible with simplicial operators. It is fibrant when every simplicial mapping set is a Kan complex. Every small space $X$ admits a small fibrant simplicial groupoid $G$ and an equivalence $N_{\mathrm{hc}}G\simeq X$.

source.place: Remark 4.2.5, citing Dwyer–Kan, Homotopy theory and simplicial groupoids, Theorems 2.5 and 3.3 (existence of a fibrant strict simplicial-groupoid model for every space). Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Represent the given small space by its Kan complex $X$, and put $A=\mathfrak C[X]$. In the Joyal model structure $\varnothing\to X$ is a monomorphism, hence a cofibration. The left Quillen functor $\mathfrak C$ preserves this initial map and cofibrations, so $A$ is Bergner-cofibrant. The derived unit of the Quillen equivalence gives $X\simeq\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}(A)=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(RA)$. This last nerve is itself Kan. The mapping-space and composition comparisons identify its homotopy category with $\pi_0(RA)$. The derived-unit map is the identity on vertices, since rigidification and $R$ keep those objects, and induces bijections on hom sets of homotopy categories. For an arrow class $a:x\to y$ in $\pi_0(RA)$, lift it along this bijection to a class $f:x\to y$ in $hX$. Filling the outer $2$-horn with edges $f$ and $\mathrm{id}_x$ gives a left inverse $g$, and filling the other outer $2$-horn with $f$ and $\mathrm{id}_y$ gives a right inverse $h$. In $hX$ these coincide because $g=g(fh)=(gf)h=h$. The image of $g$ is therefore a two-sided inverse of $a$, so $\pi_0(RA)$ is a groupoid. The Kan conclusion now follows from the locally Kan/groupoid clause of the coherent-nerve comparison. Thus the derived unit is an equivalence between spaces, not merely between arbitrary quasicategories.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1 and its proof, printed pp.89-92; Proposition 1.2.5.1; derived-unit computation as in Appendix A.2.5.

proof.text: Let $O=\operatorname{Ob}A$, and form the degreewise ordinary groupoid completion $B=A[A^{-1}]$ with this same object set. Every simplicial operator on $A$ extends uniquely to $B$, sending each formal inverse to the inverse of the image, so $B$ is a strict simplicial groupoid with constant objects. Apply the total-inversion clause of [lem-coef-cofibrant-simplicial-inversion] to the cofibrant pair $A\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}A$ on $O$; the identity is a cofibration. It gives a weak homotopy equivalence $\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}(A)\to\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}(B)$ and says that the target is Kan. There is no assumption here that the original mapping sets of $A$ were Kan.

source.place: Sections 9.1-9.2, printed p.279; use the existing coherent-nerve formulation of cofibrant inversion.

proof.text: Write $F=\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}$. Keep $O$ as object set and define $G(x,y)=F(B(x,y))$. If $c_{P,Q}:F(P\times Q)\xrightarrow{\cong}FP\times FQ$ and $c_0:F(*)\xrightarrow{\cong}*$ are the canonical comparisons, define composition by $F(m)\circ c_{P,Q}^{-1}$, identities by $F(e_x)\circ c_0^{-1}$, and inversion by $F(i_{x,y}):F(B(x,y))\to F(B(y,x))$. These operations satisfy the strict groupoid equations: after the canonical product comparisons, associativity is $F(m\circ(m\times1))=F(m\circ(1\times m))$, and the two inverse equations are the images of $m(i(a),a)=e$ and $m(a,i(a))=e$. The unit equations are also preserved: writing $e_x:*\to B(x,x)$ and $p:B(x,y)\to *$, the original equations are $m\circ\langle e_y p,\mathrm{id}\rangle=\mathrm{id}$ and $m\circ\langle\mathrm{id},e_x p\rangle=\mathrm{id}$, and applying $F$ gives the corresponding two equations on $G(x,y)$. Product projections and diagonals are preserved by the canonical comparisons; their iterated comparisons agree because their projections agree. Thus the displayed associative, unit, and inverse equations are equalities of simplicial maps. Consequently every degree of $G$ is an ordinary groupoid and all its simplicial operators preserve inverses.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.6.4: preservation of finite limits, applied to the composition, identity and inverse equations.

proof.text: For each ordered pair $(x,y)$, the Kan-replacement theorem makes $G(x,y)$ Kan and makes $B(x,y)\to G(x,y)$ a weak homotopy equivalence. Naturality of this unit, including its compatibility with the canonical product comparisons, makes these maps an enriched functor $u:B\to G$ identity on $O$. Its map on each hom set of $\pi_0$ is bijective and its object map is the identity, so $\pi_0u$ is an equivalence. Thus $u$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. This also proves that $G$ is fibrant in the meaning required by the item.

source.place: Construction 3.3.6.1 and Propositions 3.3.6.4, 3.3.6.7, 3.3.6.9; the Dwyer--Kan condition is the definition in the cited comparison node.

proof.text: The derived coherent nerve inverts the Dwyer--Kan equivalence $u$, giving $\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}(B)\simeq\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}(G)$. Since $G$ is already locally Kan, the right-derived-functor calculation may use $G$ itself as fibrant replacement, giving $\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}(G)\simeq N_{\mathrm{hc}}G$; this does not assert that the specified functor $R$ literally fixes $G$. Each arrow of $\pi_0G$ has the inverse induced by the strict inverse in degree zero. Hence $\pi_0G$ is a groupoid and the coherent-nerve comparison says that $N_{\mathrm{hc}}G$ is Kan. These comparisons are therefore equivalences between spaces.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1; Proposition 1.2.5.1; Appendix A.2.5, computation of the right derived functor on fibrant objects.

proof.text: Combining the preceding equivalences of spaces gives $X\simeq\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}(A)\simeq\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}(B)\simeq N_{\mathrm{hc}}G$, and invert the composite to obtain the requested equivalence. All constructions stay in $\mathcal U$: $\mathfrak C[X]$ is the colimit over the small set of simplices of $X$ of its small simplex rigidifications; each groupoid completion uses finite signed words in small arrow sets and a quotient; each $F(B(x,y))$ uses maps out of finite subdivided simplices and a countable colimit. The object set remains the small set $O$. For $X=\varnothing$ all three categories are empty and the conclusion is the identity on the empty space. No basepoint, connectedness, or nonempty mapping-set assumption was used.

source.place: Remark 4.2.5, existence conclusion; universe bookkeeping for the explicit construction in steps 1-5.

proof_origin.place: Remark 4.2.5, existence of fibrant simplicial-groupoid models, proved here from the existing cofibrant-inversion, coherent-nerve and Ex-infinity nodes rather than restated as a new model-equivalence node.
